# Translation of Sumerian Text

This appears to be a mythological or cosmological composition. Here's a translation attempt:

1. From the first day, from that day of heaven and earth, [it was created]
2. From the first night, from that night of heaven and earth, [it was created]
3. [From] the first year, the year [of] fate [was determined]
4. The [great] ones were born
5. The lady Inana possessed the divine office
6. The lady Inana—heaven and earth—was made to overflow
7. The lady Inana [....] was fashioned—birth occurred
8. The gods in assembly—their [place] was bound to the [assembly hall]
9. The great gods, doing their work—the small gods carrying burdens, bore them
10. The gods who draw water—they heaped up (the) dirt
11. The gods who carry mud—they established their life (through) word
12. That day, the wide ear—the mud of the great gods was present
13. Enki from the Apsû—the dais, the place of the gods—its interior was not known
14. Its sleeping place they did not sleep; water, food—they could not be taken
15. The gods weeping—they made lamentation; they acted in sorrow
16. To the man of food, to the one who sleeps—the sleeping place could not be taken
17. Nammu, mother who gave birth—to the great gods
18. Sorrow—the gods—their children were brought
19-20. [Fragmentary lines regarding sleep and fate]
21. The creator, whose hand fashions—its [....] was seized

**Note:** This translation is provisional, as some signs are partially preserved or ambiguous.
